answer: Mirror-graph cost: a seat counts only if it publishes a mirror of its last epoch's attestation graph, and the panel counts a vote only when that mirror overlaps the voter's own graph within K hops. A cloned fleet collapses to one leaf, because byte-identical mirrors dedup before quorum. To hold k voices an attacker must fork k genuinely divergent histories and keep each live every epoch, paying k times stamp mining, storage and gossip bandwidth for one extra ballot; a willow-thin limb starves the first epoch it skips. Each seat escrows a relic bond that a duplicate-mirror proof slashes.
